page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.18xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 72 vCPUs and 36 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by a 320 MB L3 cache and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance is equipped with 576.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core.

A defining characteristic of this instance is its bundled local storage, consisting of 45,000 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. This massive local storage volume is paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 38 Gbps. The combination of high-capacity local NVMe storage and high-speed DDR5 memory makes the instance highly resource-dense, offering a qualitative cost-efficiency advantage for workloads requiring massive local data footprints without relying on external block storage.

In benchmark testing, the i7ie.18xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 69,824.62 and a PassMark CPU score of 82,956.08. Memory bandwidth is also strong, reaching 287.15 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 120.7 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Database operations are highly efficient, as evidenced by a PassMark database score of 32,734.62 and a Redis SET throughput of 91.92 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput is top-tier, reaching 109.44 GB/sec.

While the instance excels in multi-threaded tasks, database operations, and high-throughput web serving, its single-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2,122.1. Additionally, without dedicated GPU hardware, large-scale LLM text generation is limited, as shown by an average 4.3 tokens per second on a 70B model. This instance is best suited for large-scale relational and non-relational databases, data warehousing, high-throughput web serving, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines that require direct access to massive local NVMe storage.
